captions.detailed: A 3D model of a cross-slide drill-press vise consisting of a dark blue base plate, an intermediate sliding saddle, and a top jaw body. The saddle slides linearly along the X-axis on light gray dovetail ways, while the top jaw body slides along the Y-axis on its own set of ways. Two silver-ringed crank handles with dark shafts are present to control each sliding axis independently.
captions.instruction: Generate a 3D model of a cross-slide drill-press vise. The design must feature a dark blue base plate with light gray dovetail ways, a middle saddle that translates along the X-axis, and a top jaw body that translates along the Y-axis. Include two rotatable silver crank handles on lead-screw shafts to control the movement of each sliding axis.
captions.factory: The code constructs the assembly using primitive boxes and cylinders. The base plate is created from a flat box, combined with extruded prism shapes representing the dovetail ways. The intermediate saddle and top jaw body are built similarly with complementary slot cutouts and guide rails. Crank handles are modeled by combining a cylinder for the shaft, a thin ring/torus approximation for the wheel, and a small handle pin. Prismatic joints are defined for the X and Y translations, and continuous revolute joints are assigned to the two crank handles.
